dataset_build.reproducibility_check: build-dataset re-run with --force produced an identical manifest_hash

training.early_stop_reason: not triggered: val_nll improved monotonically every epoch, patience=5 never exceeded, ran the full configured 20 epochs

resume_drill.method: SIGINT sent to the training subprocess only after a bounded (20s deadline, 0.05s interval) poll of run_manifest.json observed phase_statuses.train == RUNNING -- no fixed sleep
resume_drill.resume_result: train completed to epoch 20/20, then export, evaluate, screen, package, verify all ran and completed within the same resume invocation

screening_fixture_harness.note: the pipeline's built-in `screen` phase is a synthetic fixture harness by design; it measures legality/fallback only, never win/loss (docs/offline-training-v1.md). It is not the real-match evaluation used for this pilot's Rule-v0 comparison -- see paired_evaluation below.

export_and_package.dist_publish_note: dist/kaggle/neural-student-v1/ is a single shared, non-run-scoped publish path hardcoded in cli.py's _publish_dist(); it is overwritten by ANY subsequent full offline-training pipeline run in this worktree, including ones executed by the test suite (e.g. tests/test_offline_training_v1.py::test_signal_interruption_and_resume). It must not be treated as stable pilot evidence. The run-scoped package directory under runs/offline-training-v1/<run-id>/package/ is authoritative and was confirmed unchanged (model_hash matches run_manifest.json) after the full regression suite ran.

clean_room_verify.fallback_cases_note: 2 of 8 cases intentionally exercise the missing-model fallback lane inside the same clean-room subprocess; this is a deliberate negative test, not an unexpected fallback.

new_evaluation_glue_code.reason: no existing tool could run a real Rule-v0-vs-neural-Student-v1 actual-cabt match: the pipeline's own `screen` command is a fixture-only legality harness (never measures win/loss even when actual cabt is available), and the existing `student` challenger in scripts/run_actual_agent_viability.py targets the older linear C4 (StudentV0Model) artifact format, not neural-student-v1.
new_evaluation_glue_code.change: added a `neural_student` challenger to the evaluation-only actual-cabt viability harness (src/mage_ptcg/evaluation/actual_agents.py, scripts/run_actual_agent_viability.py) that loads a neural-student-v1 export via NeuralRuntimePolicy with a deterministic Rule Agent v0 fallback, mirroring the safety-boundary logic already used by the independent Kaggle package's own main.py template.
new_evaluation_glue_code.safety_boundary_preserved: main.py (the actual Kaggle submission entrypoint) was not modified. The new factory lives only in mage_ptcg.evaluation.actual_agents, a module explicitly documented as not imported by main.py, so this evaluation glue does not make the neural Student reachable from the submission surface's default agent.

paired_evaluation_combined.interpretation: no strong first/second-player bias once aggregated across both seeds (~59-60% for the champion regardless of seat); the champion's overall edge over the pilot-scale Student is the dominant, fairly seat-independent signal. The between-seed spread (50/100 vs 31/100) is within plausible binomial noise for n=100 each and is exactly why a single-seed measurement would have been misleading.

go_long_run_because: every mechanical gate passed with zero pipeline-level failures across ~330 real actual-cabt games run in this pilot (2 smoke + 128 collection + 100 preflight + 100 paired-eval): 0 crash, 0 timeout, 0 invalid action, 0 illegal action, 0 unexpected fallback
offline metrics show a reasonable, unambiguous sign that learning worked: monotonic loss/validation improvement over 20 epochs, 93.9% top-1 fidelity beating the linear baseline by 2.8 points
the pilot Student never silently degraded to Rule Agent v0 in live play (fallback_count=0 across 200 paired-evaluation games); every decision was a genuine model inference

the observed 40.5% live win rate against Rule Agent v0 (95% CI [33.9%, 47.4%]) is a real, non-trivial gap but not a catastrophic collapse, and is consistent with the known compounding-error limitation of small-scale behavior cloning (128 games, compact model, 20 epochs) rather than an infrastructure defect
not_go_long_run_reservations: GO_LONG_RUN is not a Champion promotion signal: Rule Agent v0 still wins the majority of paired games in this pilot
the long run's success criteria should explicitly target closing this win-rate gap (more collected games, more epochs/capacity, or both), not merely reproducing the pilot at larger scale

tests.full_regression_note: PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 is required in this environment: without it, a system-wide ROS `launch_testing` pytest plugin auto-loads and fails collection with ModuleNotFoundError on an unrelated repo module before any test runs. This is a pre-existing environment quirk documented at docs/evidence/offline-training-v1.md:36, not something introduced by this pilot.

This pilot's diff never touches scripts/collect_offline_training_v1_evidence.py or its test file. Interpreted as an environment-specific timing issue (0.5s timeout too tight for child-process startup latency in this sandbox), not a regression introduced by this pilot.
